title: Augmentation compatibility from computing reduction counits
statement: Let B,C,D,E be abelian categories with chosen derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let F:B→C, G:D→E, CX:B→D and CY:C→E be exact additive functors with their canonical derived localization factors [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Let RX:B→D and RY:C→E be additive, LX:D(B)→D(D) and LY:D(C)→D(E), and let cX_P:LX(QP)→Q(RX(P)) and cY_P:LY(QP)→Q(RY(P)) be specified families. Fix ordinary units uX:CX→RX and uY:CY→RY, derived units iX:D(CX)→LX and iY:D(CY)→LY, ordinary comparisons e:RX⋙G≅F⋙RY and c:CX⋙G≅F⋙CY, and a derived comparison τ:LX⋙D(G)≅D(F)⋙LY. Suppose a class of source complexes resolves every complex by a quasi-isomorphism; cY at their F-images is invertible; the representative comparison equation [def-weil-pbc-derived-reduction-comparison-formula] holds on this class; both derived units followed by these counits equal their exact localization factor followed by Q of their ordinary units; and G(uX_M) followed by e_M equals c_M followed by uY_FM for every M. Then for every K, D(G)(iX_K) followed by τ_K equals the canonical derived exact square associated to c followed by iY_D(F)K.

proof.text: The canonical derived square associated to c commutes with exact-functor localization factors. Apply the composition-factor equations to CX,G and F,CY, cancel the first composition isomorphism, and use the factor equation for the derived natural isomorphism of c.

Restrict the two natural transformations to the resolving class. Fully faithful restriction detects equality. At a representative P postcompose with LY of the exact F factor and cY_FP; this map is invertible. Apply the representative comparison equation, combine the source derived unit with cX using its normalization, and use naturality of the G localization factor. The termwise ordinary augmented square identifies the result with Q(c_P) followed by Q(uY_FP). The exact-square factor identity and the target unit normalization give the other path. Naturality of iY finishes the representative equality, hence the global equality.

theorem derivedReduction_augmentationOfCounits
    {B C D E : Type*} [Category B] [Category C] [Category D] [Category E]
    [Abelian B] [Abelian C] [Abelian D] [Abelian E]
    [HasDerivedCategory B] [HasDerivedCategory C]
    [HasDerivedCategory D] [HasDerivedCategory E]
    (F : B ⥤ C) (G : D ⥤ E) (RX CX : B ⥤ D) (RY CY : C ⥤ E)
    [F.Additive] [G.Additive] [RX.Additive] [RY.Additive]
    [CX.Additive] [CY.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteColimits F]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits G] [PreservesFiniteColimits G]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits CX] [PreservesFiniteColimits CX]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits CY] [PreservesFiniteColimits CY]
    (LX : DerivedCategory B ⥤ DerivedCategory D)
    (LY : DerivedCategory C ⥤ DerivedCategory E)
    (cX : ∀ P : CochainComplex B ℤ, LX.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((RX.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P))
    (cY : ∀ P : CochainComplex C ℤ, LY.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((RY.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P))
    (uX : CX ⟶ RX) (uY : CY ⟶ RY)
    (iX : CX.mapDerivedCategory ⟶ LX) (iY : CY.mapDerivedCategory ⟶ LY)
    (e : RX ⋙ G ≅ F ⋙ RY) (c : CX ⋙ G ≅ F ⋙ CY)
    (τ : LX ⋙ G.mapDerivedCategory ≅ F.mapDerivedCategory ⋙ LY)
    (good : ObjectProperty (CochainComplex B ℤ))
    (res : ∀ K, ∃ (P : CochainComplex B ℤ) (p : P ⟶ K), good P ∧ QuasiIso p)
    (hiso : ∀ P, good P → IsIso (cY ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)))
    (hnorm : ∀ P, good P →
      DerivedReductionComparisonFormula F G RX RY LX LY cX cY e τ P)
    (hX : ∀ P, good P → iX.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ≫ cX P =
      CX.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app P ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map ((NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex uX (.up ℤ)).app P))
    (hY : ∀ P, good P →
      iY.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)) ≫
        cY ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) =
      CY.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map ((NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex uY (.up ℤ)).app
          ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)))
    (hOrd : ∀ M, G.map (uX.app M) ≫ e.hom.app M = c.hom.app M ≫ uY.app (F.obj M)) :
    ∀ K : DerivedCategory B,
      G.mapDerivedCategory.map (iX.app K) ≫ τ.hom.app K =
        ((Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso CX G).symm ≪≫
          Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso c ≪≫
            Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso F CY).hom.app K ≫
          iY.app (F.mapDerivedCategory.obj K)
